HRA Analysis: OVERVIEW:MAURLEN COMPASS (2) isn't blessed with gate speed but has been finishing her races off well and drops back significantly in class after a decent performance against much stronger opposition in the Oaks. She'll need to map reasonably well over the distance, but she should appreciate this level and get the chance to show her class in a suitable race. MAJOR ORION (3) is a quick beginner and looks likely to cross to the pegs and lead these, which is a big advantage at Echuca, particularly over the short trip. He put in a bad run two starts back, but that was an outlier in what's been a very good season for him. He's had only one start at this track for a win, and although this is slightly harder, he'll take some catching. OWEN THE SAINTS (8) was a good winner last week when able to lead all the way at Shepparton but goes from the front to the back row now, with a few strong runners drawn ahead of him. He must still be respected. WICKED MITZI (5) found a decent draw last time and was able to put her best foot forward in a much stronger race. She draws a little awkwardly but is a winner at this track, which is a plus. OUR CHEEKY DEVIL (1), MISTER JIMARINGLE (4) and LINE DANCE (7) can all map reasonably well and have minor claims. BACK: MAURLEN COMPASS (2) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:MAURLEN COMPASS (2), MAJOR ORION (3), OWEN THE SAINTS (8), WICKED MITZI (5)

OVERVIEW:MUSSEL SHOALS (3) gets a great draw to find the front here, a position where she always delivers her best performances. She led last time over this trip, but that was a much stronger race where she was forced to run a fast time, and she seems less likely to face the same pressure here. She has a good record at this track and will take some catching. WHERES WOOD WOOD (7) is racing in career-best form, and even though she's missed a place in her past three starts, she's still raced honestly. This is her home track, and she loves it here, so while she'll need luck from the draw, she's a strong chance. FLIP A COIN (1) is first up and doesn't have great numerical form, but his best efforts last preparation have him well in this, and he draws to map softly. TALKNPLAY (9) has been in career-best form this preparation, winning three from four. It's a different challenge now from the back row and against some in-form types, but he's in the mix. ARMOURY (6) has been racing well in two runs for the new stable, so keep him safe despite the draw. EEBEEBEE (8) is fitter second up and might be worth considering for the minor money, trailing through off the back row. BACK: MUSSEL SHOALS (3) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:MUSSEL SHOALS (3), WHERES WOOD WOOD (7), FLIP A COIN (1), TALKNPLAY (9)

OVERVIEW:ALTO CORAGGIO (4) has been runner-up in all five career starts, and surely tonight's the night he breaks through for a victory. While he led and had his chance last week, the winner might be pretty good, and you can make a case that he's run well in all his narrow defeats. He looks likely to find the lead here, take control and won't find a more suitable race to break his maiden. THE PRIVATE DEAL (1) will need a scratching to get into the field. He's had three runs for the new stable and has earned market respect despite not looking well suited in most of those races. He now gets a draw and the right opposition to make an impact. He may be a bit tricky at the start, but if he's safely away, he'll be a threat. CARTIMANDUA (2) draws softly with a good driver, and while she'll need to improve on recent efforts, that map prominence will help in a race like this. Likewise for ALCATRAZ MISS (3), a 39-start maiden who's been getting closer in her past few. RISE AGAIN (6) goes to the astute Ashwood stable, which can improve these lower-rated types quickly, so watch the betting. BACK: ALTO CORAGGIO (4) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS:ALTO CORAGGIO (4), THE PRIVATE DEAL (1), RISE AGAIN (6), CARTIMANDUA (2)

OVERVIEW:SPIRIT OF SPITFIRE (3) is a fascinating runner, being a former New Zealander who had two trials in NSW, switched stables, had a run in Adelaide with a solid SP and now races here with top driver James Herbertson booked. No question she'll attract plenty of market interest, and while you're guessing a bit with what's exposed, the positive indicators suggest she's a strong chance. MAURLEN GRACE (4) was held up badly last week. She was buried back after being slow to begin before galloping when looking a strong chance along the passing lane. There appears to be improvement this preparation, so she's a chance again. ASHANTE WARRIOR (9) has found good form for the Ashwood stable, winning last week in a suitable race, but the draw makes things harder this time. FRESH PRINCE (1) has his second run for the Carbone stable, and while he'll need to lift on that first-up effort, the draw offers a chance to atone. CALIVIL (8) is first up since February and has won a trial leading into this. I'd prefer his chances with more fitness, but don't dismiss him entirely. SELECTIONS:SPIRIT OF SPITFIRE (3), MAURLEN GRACE (4), ASHANTE WARRIOR (9), FRESH PRINCE (1)

OVERVIEW: A tricky start to the Quaddie, with several of these trotters either not in peak form or with fitness to come. FARSTAR (4) goes back to the front row and a draw that saw him lead and win three runs back at Shepparton, albeit in slow time. Having top driver Mark Pitt aboard gives confidence he'll be hard to beat against these. SAINT EYES (2) has gone close in his past couple of runs and draws softly to be in the mix again. His last win in April saw him beat stronger types than he meets now. ITS DIAMOND CREEK (5) is first up for over a year with two trials under his belt and a stable switch back to former trainer Jenny Johnson. He has gate speed and did seem to be nearing another win last preparation. LITTLE TEDEY (6) drops back in class, while ALDEBARAN MARCUS (3) also doesn't tend to win out of turn, but both are worth consideration. SELECTIONS:FARSTAR (4), SAINT EYES (2), ITS DIAMOND CREEK (5), LITTLE TEDEY (6)

OVERVIEW:COLBY ART (8) drops back significantly in class here and has been good in three runs for the new stable. He was a winner two starts back when starting off the back row, scoring in a time that would be good enough to cover these. He trails through behind a speedy beginner, so he shouldn't map too far off them. LORIMERMAJOR (7) likewise finds a more suitable race but hasn't won since the start of the year, although he's been runner-up six times. He has a tricky draw to overcome, but his form is better than most. BERYLS BOOTS (4) goes to the front row and has been much better this season. He'll need some luck with the map, but if he gets cover, he'll be thereabouts. TEMPTING TIGER (1) and POLLY PEACHUM (2) can map softly from their draws but are up in class and have minor claims, while YELLA (5) has burned my fingers too many times. Although he looks suited again, I'd prefer to see him step up before getting involved. BACK: COLBY ART (8) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS:COLBY ART (8), LORIMERMAJOR (7), BERYLS BOOTS (4), TEMPTING TIGER (1)

OVERVIEW:CADENCE LANE (4) likes the standing-start conditions and may find this more suitable than recent outings. Her last win came from the tapes in Adelaide, where she was able to lead, and James Herbertson going aboard only adds confidence to her chances from what appears a suitable map. STARLIGHT RED (2) is a veteran mare suited by the front-row draw and standing-start conditions. She's likely to take up the running around the tighter-turning Echuca track, which is to her advantage given she races well here. Her only win this season came at this track and distance, so she'll give plenty of cheek for a long way. SUZYS DREAM (5) has a strong SP profile this preparation and has been racing consistently, including two seconds at this track. It's a slight concern she's yet to place under standing-start conditions, but her form is better than most. VAN DOREN (6) is her stablemate and does appreciate this track and the conditions. While the numerical form doesn't appeal, the drop in class does suit. MISS AVENGER (1) could have claims for the minor money if she gets away safely. SELECTIONS:CADENCE LANE (4), STARLIGHT RED (2), SUZYS DREAM (5), VAN DOREN (6)

OVERVIEW:ARRAPS (7) normally likes to lead in his races, so won't get that opportunity from this awkward draw, but his current form is hard to overlook in this moderate line-up. He's gone close in better races with a strong SP profile in his past four starts, so while he'll need some luck, with clear running late he can close strongly. ESERANZA (2) can improve sharply on her current form, reunited with Herbertson, as the pair combined for a close 2nd four runs back when able to find the lead from a wider draw than she has here. She can control things from the top end and take plenty of running down. ICANMOTOR (4) narrowly missed two starts ago when runner-up, and while he has a tricky draw, a good driver helps negate that. He can be a threat coming with one run. JOEYS HANGOVER (6) will find this grade more to his liking after mixing his form against stronger types. The draw makes things tricky, but keep him safe. BEYONDREASON (1) is hard to take on form but does get a stable switch and a soft draw, so is worth taking on trust. SELECTIONS:ARRAPS (7), ESERANZA (2), ICANMOTOR (4), JOEYS HANGOVER (6)

OVERVIEW:THEBUCKSONYOU (8) is a handy 4yo pacer, which is resuming since a fifth at Mildura in August. He is versatile and beat a reasonable field at a Swan Hill victory towards the end of his last campaign so he must be respected. SHIRLEY NOT (7) won twice at Mildura in October and has the perfect trailing draw behind MIDNIGHT PIRATE (1) so she cannot be left out of calculations. She was held up for a run at a vital stage and chased hard for second on Thursday night. MIDNIGHT PIRATE (1) defeated an easier field on Thursday night but he kicked well clear at the 400m and sustained the run so he is worth thought from the pole position. MAGGACIS (2) endured a wide trip in the final circuit and battled on well when resuming on Thursday night. He should be fitter and is better drawn so he is not without a chance. SELECTIONS: THEBUCKSONYOU (8), SHIRLEY NOT (7), MIDNIGHT PIRATE (1), MAGGACIS (2)

OVERVIEW:THE LADYBIRD (11) settled in the second half of the field, angled wide in the home straight and finished off quickly for an eye-catching third at Shepparton last week. She gained a nice trail and got home best to win at Mildura prior so she is worth thought again. THE IRISHMAN (8) has been placed at his past four attempts and should be competitive against this class. He raced without cover throughout and battled on strongly for third at Mount Gambier last outing. PUNTO CALIENTE (7) ran home strongly from last and did well at Mildura on Thursday night. He is awkwardly drawn but should be hitting the line strongly again. WATCHING OVER US (6) finished off well for second behind THE LADYBIRD (11) on November 10. He was driven very aggressively in the early stages and peaked at the end on Thursday night but his efforts from off the speed prior were sound. DIAMOND KRUSHER (5) and GROVE DALE (2) are both fast beginners and are drawn to be prominent over sprint distance. SELECTIONS: THE LADYBIRD (11), THE IRISHMAN (8), PUNTO CALIENTE (7), WATCHING OVER US (6)

OVERVIEW: DALLAS MIKI (7) is a strong staying type that performs best when he is able to lead so he couldn’t have drawn worse. He progressed forward to find the front and dominated his rivals two starts ago and he has the class to test this field. He was gunned down by KYORETSU (8) on Thursday night but the extra distance of this event is in his favour. KYORETSU (8) began quickly, raced roughly and did well to remain pacing on the first turn to trail the leader and was very quick at the end when he won on Thursday night. He drops back to the second line now but should prove hard to beat again. NAROBI (2) is a South Australian trained mare that is making her Mildura debut. She has been racing consistently and trainer Peter Bain boasts a good strike rate at Mildura so she must be respected. PRIORITISE (6) sustained a long run to beat a field of similar quality on October 20. He has had a horror run with the barrier draw but he was placed under similar conditions on Thursday night and continues to perform strongly so he cannot be dismissed. SELECTIONS: DALLAS MIKI (7), KYORETSU (8), NAROBI (2), PRIORITISE (6)

OVERVIEW: SPRINGFIELD RIVER (6) joins trainer John Tormey and will appreciate a significant drop back in class for this assignment. He is versatile and is capable of running fast time so he warrants respect. CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (3) attempted to lead throughout when second at Mildura on Thursday night. He is drawn to obtain a prominent position again and looms as one of the leading chances. ACCELERE (5) is a fast beginner and performs best when he is able to lead. He has created a good impression at Mildura with a string of consistent performances and another bold showing is expected. He left a trailing position to park without cover and didn’t have a great deal of luck on Thursday night. ROJENBYE (1) finished off solidly from midfield to get up and defeat My Ultimate Rudi at Mildura on November 06. He is likely to gain an economical run from the ideal draw and is worth thought again, despite performing well below expectations on Thursday night. BACK: SPRINGFIELD RIVER (6) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: SPRINGFIELD RIVER (6), CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (3), ACCELERE (5), ROJENBYE (1)

OVERVIEW:CAULONIA TERROR (4) is capable of sprinting to the line quickly with the right trail forward as evidenced by his big victory at Mildura on Thursday night. He has struck peak form and will take beating again. OZZIE DAYBREAK (7) has been racing well but without luck and gets his chance to run a big race with the perfect trailing draw behind the likely leader HOOKLINEANDSINKER (1). He performed nicely again on Thursday night having worked into third at the end. G B BRAVE (3) ran home nicely for a game second when resuming on Thursday night and is worth a ticket each way. CALF PEN (5) ran a big race when he moved up without cover and went down fighting when second behind Bettorbust on November 06. He was driven aggressively early and raced fiercely thereafter so he had excuses on Thursday night. He continues to perform strongly against this class and should give another bold showing. HOOKLINEANDSINKER (1) hasn’t been at his best form recently but he tends to excel when he is able to lead over the sprint distance so he has the conditions to suit him here. SELECTIONS: CAULONIA TERROR (4), OZZIE DAYBREAK (7),G B BRAVE (3), CALF PEN (5)

OVERVIEW:EVA EXPRESS (6) led out then took cover when a close second behind Mystic Motiver in a stronger race at Kilmore two starts ago. She was caught wide early and had to be restrained to last from a similar poor draw on Thursday night but will find this to be a suitable assignment and should take tossing. SWEET LUCY LOU (5) possesses early speed and is a good chance of finding the lead. She raced without cover throughout at her latest fourth and should be competitive against this line up. LITLMAX (7) was confidently driven and showed promise when second on debut. She didn’t have much luck at her next few attempts and went down fighting after racing without cover on Thursday night so she could gain her maiden success at short notice. DARK AT MIDNIGHT (3) is a first starter for trainer Andrew Vozlic, which finished a distant third at his only trial performance. He is nicely drawn first up so he must be kept safe. SELECTIONS: EVA EXPRESS (6), SWEET LUCY LOU (5), LITLMAX (7), DARK AT MIDNIGHT (3)

OVERVIEW: OUR MONARCH (5) was heavily supported and was run down in the last stride when attempting to lead throughout at her debut performance. She should have benefited from that experience and is capable of going one better. BETTY CAROLINE (2) left the position behind the leader to race without cover when a brave second at Mildura last week. She is ideally drawn and should run a big race again. CRUEL MISTRESS (7) is an experienced maiden having had 33 attempts but she is getting closer to the money. She raced without cover when a game second behind Cheddar Cheese on November 06 and was the runner up again at Mildura on Thursday night. SANTA CASA LEVI (3) was checked with 700m remaining and lost approximately four lengths when unplaced on Thursday night and is a possible improver from his good draw. BACK: OUR MONARCH (5) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: OUR MONARCH (5), BETTY CAROLINE (2), CRUEL MISTRESS (7), SANTA CASA LEVI (3)

OVERVIEW: WINSHEMAY (3) followed some good trial performances with a soft debut victory then was spelled. She finished strongly from a long way back when third on resumption and she appears to have a promising future. MY ULTIMATE HENRY (5) progressed forward to find the lead, ran along at a genuine tempo and was run down late in fast time on Thursday night. He is racing well and looms as one of the leading chances again. SHUDABOUGHTABOAT (6) has done well in three local starts and should make his presence felt. He was a runaway winner on November 06 then attempted to lead throughout and was run down by the handy South Australian pacer Hilltop Crunch at his latest second. TAMALIA (1) was placed after trailing the leader at St Arnaud on November 08 and she led throughout to beat easier opposition on Thursday night. She is drawn to suit her racing pattern and may be able to take the next step forward. KAIDENBOY (2) makes his debut for trainer Kate Attard and took on a stronger field at his latest Ararat fifth. He has claims along with CLARENDEN ARCADIA (4). BACK: WINSHEMAY (3) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: WINSHEMAY (3), MY ULTIMATE HENRY (5), SHUDABOUGHTABOAT (6), TAMALIA (1)

OVERVIEW: HESASTAR (6) is the one of only two horses in this event that did not contest the meeting at Mildura on Thursday so he comes into the race with fresh legs. He was driven aggressively from the same draw and was able to score after racing without cover throughout in a field of similar quality last outing so he will prove very hard to beat again. EAGLEYE (4) was a late withdrawal on Thursday night but his overall form has been sound and he strikes a suitable assignment now. INDIANAS SON (5) settled midfield and held his ground over the latter stages at Mildura on Thursday. The small field will assist his chances and he is capable of filling a place. THE DEVIL ROLLS ON (3) was driven for early speed but couldn’t get across to the markers and was shuffled back in the field mid-race so he didn’t enjoy the best of luck at Mildura on Thursday. He gets his chance to improve under these conditions. THE AFRICAN QUEEN (2) gained a nice trail and battled into a distant fourth on Thursday night. She is a place chance from her good draw. BACK: HESASTAR (6) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: HESASTAR (6), EAGLEYE (4), INDIANAS SON (5), THE DEVIL ROLLS ON (3)

OVERVIEW: This is a competitive race to open the card, with a case that can be made for each horse. MONARO DEAN (3) is a former New Zealand trotter who has had just eight career starts, all from stand starts, for one victory. That win came early in his career over the 2600-metre trip on a grass track. On that occasion, he flashed home from the back of the field to win late. His last start in New Zealand was a second on the grass. He is now in the care of Andy Gath. He had a mobile trial at Melton, where he was slightly off the arm but got away okay. He won the trial by a big margin in slow time. He looks like a nice horse, but this is a very different style of racing to what he is used to. RAMBO SUFFARELL (4) is a better horse than his numerical form suggests. His last start was in March, when he got well back and flashed home nicely. His other prior runs were either unlucky or he got his manners wrong. He is first-up here, but he has some ability. FONDA RHONDA (10) has a nice turn of foot and can be a decent swooper late when saved for one run. Last start, she was first-up at Cranbourne and finished second after racing in the breeze for the last lap. Likely to improve again with fitness. SPIRITED GIGI (7) is a smart trotter who has raced competitively throughout his career against the top horses in his age group. A sticky barrier here. Also respecting the D’Arne Bellman-trained duo especially RAPTA (4).SHEZALOVER (9) and CHANTILLY LASS (2) are winning chances also. SELECTIONS: MONARO DEAN (3), RAMBO SUFFARELL (4), FONDA RHONDA (10), SPIRITED GIGI (7)

OVERVIEW:THE FASHIONISTA (10) has a strong last 800-metre sprint. She is first-up here for Andy Gath and finished second in a recent trial behind Coconut Mickey. Expecting a good performance here, but the wide back-row barrier is a concern. DREAMS OF LOVE (4) has been racing well and has found some of her best form since joining the Kaylene Ward stable. She won well after leading two starts ago at Ballarat and has since gone for a spell. At her best, she’s a winning chance here, although fitness will be a query. KALARNEY PRINCE (3) is a flashy grey trotter who is hard to miss. He doesn’t win often, but rarely runs a bad race. He will need to map well here for luck to be in his favour. ALLWATFUNJINGLES (1) has good gate speed and the ace barrier to use to his advantage here. BACK: THE FASHIONISTA (10)– 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: THE FASHIONISTA (10), DREAMS OF LOVE (4), KALARNEY PRINCE (3), ALLWATFUNJINGLES (1)

OVERVIEW: This is another very competitive event with many winning chances. KYVALLEY DAYTONA (10) is having her third career start. On debut, she finished third at Maryborough after flashing home nicely. Last start, she got it wrong with her manners. Since then, she has won a slow trial at Kilmore. She looks to be a nice type when she puts it all together. TRUE APLOMB (3) is a well-bred filly who has promise but can get it wrong with her manners. Last start, however, she did everything right and finished second at Maryborough behind the smart Jilliby Connection. She chased determinedly there and gapped the other rivals behind her. DELIGHTFUL REYNA (1) has the best barrier she has had since early in her career. She has been racing okay, but with a positive race map here, she finds a chance to turn her form around. ALDEBARAN BOBBY (4) is a first starter for Jodi Quinlan. He let down well in a recent trial behind the older horse Night Flight. We will learn more about him here. BACK: KYVALLEY DAYTONA (10)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: KYVALLEY DAYTONA (10), TRUE APLOMB (3), DELIGHTFUL REYNA (1), ALDEBARAN BOBBY (4)

OVERVIEW:HIGHVIEW HAMMER (2) was an okay second last start when leading. He is first-up here for Samantha Gangell. He has fantastic gate speed and should be able to find the fence. SPORTS WRACK (6) is an experienced horse who is versatile and rarely runs a bad race. He got back into the winner’s circle two starts ago when leading at Charlton. The barrier is sticky, but he is the type of horse who can sometimes make his own luck. ZEUSS (5) is an interesting runner here. He is fourth-up for Rebecca Bartley and is having his first look at the Melton track. He has flashed home to win his last two starts impressively. An awkward barrier, but his last two starts have also been from tricky starting positions. KIMCHI (4) has been in great form recently, racing at his best and putting together good performances. This is harder, though. BACK: HIGHVIEW HAMMER (2)– 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: HIGHVIEW HAMMER (2), SPORTS WRACK (6), ZEUSS (5), KIMCHI (4)

OVERVIEW:TED BEAR (7) has a great turn of foot when he is saved for one run. His race map is likely to be tricky here from the sticky barrier, but he’s a nice horse who is racing well. AUSSIE JAY MAC (8) is the only horse on the second row, so he has options with his race map. However, there are some concerns with his manners, as he has occasionally galloped in his runs. He seems to be okay when he’s in front, which he won’t be here from barrier eight. LIBERTY STAR DUST (6) was a good second last start at Cranbourne. He worked forward, raced in the breeze and battled on well for second. He will need some luck here from the barrier. TOMBEUR (1) looks to be a smart performer who is still learning what racing is all about. He’s had three career starts. He won on debut, then had to race tough in his second start but still ran well for fourth. Last start, he got it wrong with his manners. If he does everything right and can hold a forward position, he’s a big threat from the fence. SELECTIONS: TED BEAR (7), AUSSIE JAY MAC (8), LIBERTY STAR DUST (6), TOMBEUR (1)

OVERVIEW:TEX GOES BANG (7) finished fifth last start, beaten 8.5 metres. However, he was racing in the breeze and covered an extra 31 metres by being off the fence. This race looks a little easier. He will need some luck, but James Herbertson takes the reins. He’s the best driver in Australia and knows how to find luck. MISSMALACHITE (8) is ultra-consistent and has only missed a place once in her last seven starts. She has map options as the only horse on the back row and will be flashing home here. NORTHERN TERROR (2) ran a good third last start. He settled near last, made a three-wide run and raced in the breeze, covering an extra 26 metres off the fence. He was beaten only three metres. Barrier two suits. STELLAR QUEEN (3) rarely runs a bad race, although she’s only won three times in her long career. She will need some luck, but she can run home well if saved for one run. SELECTIONS: TEX GOES BANG (7), MISSMALACHITE (8), NORTHERN TERROR (2), STELLAR QUEEN (3)

OVERVIEW:MAJOR MAURIE (5) was smashing the line impressively last start, first-up for John and Ewa Justice, but was just held up and left it too late to win. It appeared to be an improved performance and I’m looking for him to race well again here. JILLIBY UTAH (3) led and won well to break through for his maiden victory at Melton last start in rain-affected conditions. With the right run, he can run a good race again here, now with the winning confidence. ALCATRAZ GIRL (1) doesn't have great numerical form, but she has the gate speed to map well here from the ace. LIVERMERE (4) is a consistent mare who is racing well. She does have good gate speed, which she may opt to use here, or she could save her speed for one run at the end. BACK: MAJOR MAURIE (5)– 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: MAJOR MAURIE (5), JILLIBY UTAH (3), ALCATRAZ GIRL (1), LIVERMERE (4)

OVERVIEW: What a cracking race this is, one you often see on a Saturday night. Top free-for-all pacer YAMBUKIAN (6) is fourth-up here after more than a year on the sidelines, so he will be close to reaching peak race fitness. He was a brilliant second to Fox Dan in 1.51.5 two starts ago, narrowly beaten. He ran a good fourth last start in the Casey Classic in a race that was fence-dominated, while he was racing off the fence. He is class. MADIGAN (4) is a smart performer. He finished fourth last start in the St Arnaud Pacing Cup. He got home well after being held up. The map is a bit awkward, as he has some gate speed, but not as much as some of the horses around him. ISOLATION (3) was a brilliant second last start at massive odds behind Derby winner Dynamite Dan. He has great gate speed and is in career-best form. THUNDERFIRE (2) is a lightly raced horse whose talent has seen him step up to this class quite quickly. He will need some luck here, but he has ability. He may need some time to adjust to racing at this level.
